Improves on the first game in everything except performance. If you want to feel like an awesome Jedi with a world of possibilities when it comes to combat, buy this game, but make sure your PC can handle it before hand.

poor optimization caused me to wrestle with my graphics settings the entire time i was playing to try and get a decent looking game at a playable framerate.

while the new lightsaber stances are fun and the game has good enemy variety, combat feels overtuned to the point where the crossguard stance feels unusable on many enemies and the dual sabers' block cancel feels mandatory at times.

the story feels half-baked, not feeling like it hits its stride until the early endgame. it felt like the entire game could've been condensed into an act or two of a much more exciting story. the final boss especially felt like a one-note character, to the point where i could predict some of his cookie-cutter lines before he even said them. i found Skoova Stev's longwinded fisherman's tale more compelling than the main plot.

the environments were a step down from Fallen Order, feeling a lot less alien and unique than its planets.

overall, i would only recommend buying this to have context going into the inevitable third game, and i would not recommend playing it on PC.

General/Desktop: Still not perfect, but much improved since launch. I refunded this game at launch after 10 minutes because of the horrible performance and constant stuttering, but I tried it again and both have been dramatically improved. Don't get me wrong, they still have some work to do, and there is still some minor traversal stutter, but on a Ryzen 5600x at stock clocks, with RT off, I get a pretty solid 60 fps. Additionally, keep in mind that this game was made a next gen exclusive for a reason, that doesnt forgive the CPU performance issues, but it will run heavier on your GPU than games that aren't next gen exclusive; I'm able to keep 60fps at 1440p on all High (RT off) on a 6950xt, but I realize thats not what most people are running, so just keep this in mind when considering the game for your hardware.

Steam Deck: At 1280x800 with everything on Low, RT off (duh), and FSR 2 on Balanced, it's possible to get a pretty solid 30fps

Overall I did thoroughly enjoy the game and it's story, there are a few bugs I came across, but they were fixed by leaving and rejoinging the game. I'm excited for the next installment in the Fallen Order franchise, but I expect it'll take at least 5 years for the next game.

Jedi Survivor is an amazing and well made sequel to another amazing and well made game; Fallen Order. I thought that the sequel could only be as good as the first game, not better, as the first was truly a masterpiece. Little did I know that I was woefully mistaken. The sequel adds so many new mechanics and abilities, yet somehow keeping the abilities gained in the last game without making everything too confusing and complex. The addition of new fighting styles really shines, making melee combat more diverse, rather than just spamming the same old combos again and again. That all being said though, there are still serious performance issues that need to be addressed. My PC could run the first game on max settings but struggles to run this game on even the lowest settings. EA, fix your game. Please.

I've really enjoyed the Fallen Order and was looking forward to playing Survivor, given it has gathered so many rewards, but was startled by the number of negative reviews. I found out that they were mostly focusing on various bugs of the PC version ported from Consoles.
As of December 2025, I have finished the game only encountering two bugs - the game would crash after losing to a particular boss. I've been playing PC games since the 90s and am no stranger to bugs and performance issues, I thought this was alright. I own a decent last year PC, the game flies on max settings without any slowness.

The game itself is immaculately designed, well written, well acted, well paced and well structured. If you loved previous Jedi games, you would love this game!

I have to say, purchasing Star Wars Jedi: Survivor was a huge regret, and the primary culprit isn't the game itself—it's the insidious EA app launcher. Once again, EA shows their relentless dedication to sucking the joy out of gaming experiences with needless, frustrating additions. It's like EA attended the 'How to Annoy Customers 101' course and graduated with honors. Honestly, if they spent half as much time improving their games as they do creating these digital fun-suckers, we'd all be happier.

Seriously, when did navigating game launchers become a side quest? If I wanted to solve puzzles just to play a game, I'd go back to playing 'Where in the World is Carmen Sandiego?' EA, stop making gamers feel like we're stuck in a labyrinth worthy of Greek mythology. Enough with the unnecessary barriers. Gamers want immersive experiences, not another hoop to jump through! I mean, if I wanted to play a game of 'jump through pointless hoops,' I'd join a circus.

I want to start this off by saying I've beaten this game and thoroughly explored the world on ps5 so I know exactly how this game is supposed to look and feel. I'm running this game on a gtx 1080 on medium settings and it no joke runs and looks about on par with the ps5 version. Plenty of others have mentioned stutters and framerate dips, that's just apart of the jank. Jedi Outcast had it, so does this. I am using the Ultimate Engine Tweaks mod which is the most recent stability mod, so while I can't speak for how this game played without it, but with it it runs pretty damn well.

**** Recommend locking your FPS through NVIDIA control panel to 60 FPS; this way the frame drops aren't as noticeable ****

tldr.text: Mixed (69%): players like the story and characters, but many complain about bugs and crashes and poor performance.
Recent reviews are more positive at 81%, and bug complaints are rarer than before.

details.text: Complaints about bugs and crashes fell from 38% of all reviews to 21% of recent reviews, so buyers today are less likely to run into them.
Players who stayed past 50 hours are far more positive than newcomers, so first impressions tend to be harsher than long-term ones.
